mainTopic: Failed proofs in the רב–שמואל dispute about lowering versus hoisting: the two balconies, אביי's ten-טפחים principle, and the roof that needs a fixed ladder
overview: The גמרא keeps trying to settle the argument between רב and שמואל about two neighbors who share a space. One draws water easily by lowering a bucket, and the other draws with difficulty by hoisting it up. רב says they forbid each other. שמואל says the space goes to the one whose use is easy. The גמרא first brings a משנה about two balconies, one above the other. If a partition was made only for the upper one, both are forbidden without an עירוב, which seems to support רב. רב אדא בר אהבה rejects this: the lower residents climb up and lower their buckets from the upper balcony. אביי rejects it differently: the balconies are within ten טפחים of each other, so they forbid each other no matter how each one draws. The גמרא supports אביי's idea with שמואל's rule that a roof next to the רשות הרבים needs a fixed ladder. רב פפא knocks down that support, because the public may simply rest hats and scarves on the roof, so no clear proof is found for either side. The עמוד ends as a new teaching of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל begins.

steps.title: A proof from the case of two balconies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה about two balconies, one above the other. When a partition was made only for the upper one, both are forbidden until they make an עירוב. This seems to prove רב's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: There are two balconies, one above the other. A partition was made for the upper one but not for the lower one. Both are forbidden until they make an עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to try to prove רב right and שמואל wrong. The upper balcony draws water by lowering its bucket, while the lower balcony must hoist its bucket up through the upper one's opening, and the משנה still says both are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל holds that the space should be given to the side that uses it easily, which here is the upper balcony that simply lowers its bucket. So according to שמואל, the upper balcony should be permitted. Since the משנה forbids both, it seems to match רב, who says the lowering side and the hoisting side forbid each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the formula for bringing a source as proof
A balcony; here one that sticks out over water
Until they make an עירוב (join their domains)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'עשו' means they built a partition (מחיצה) of ten טפחים around the hole in the balcony floor, so water could be drawn through it on שבת. It does NOT mean they made an עירוב. The עירוב is mentioned only at the end.

phrases.english: Come and hear: two balconies
phrases.notes: This line comes from a משנה later in this פרק.

phrases.english: one above the other.
They made a partition for the upper one,
but did not make one for the lower one —
both are forbidden until they make an eruv!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: שְׁתֵּי גְזוּזְטְרָאוֹת זוֹ לְמַעְלָה מִזּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier attempts on the daf to settle the רב/שמואל dispute about lowering versus hoisting.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that a lowering user and a hoisting user forbid each other
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of two balconies one above the other, where a partition was made only for the upper one

steps.title: The lower residents climb up to draw water
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה says the משנה is about a case where the lower residents go up to the upper balcony and draw water from there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: The case is where the people of the lower balcony come up through the upper balcony to draw water.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה rejects the proof. He explains that in the משנה, the lower residents climb up and draw water from the upper balcony itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the lower residents stand on the upper balcony, then both groups draw by lowering their buckets. There is no 'easy versus hard' use here. Two equal users naturally forbid each other, so the משנה says nothing about the dispute, and שמואל can agree.

keyTerms.meaning: The residents of the lower balcony

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
It is a case where the residents of the lower balcony come
phrases.notes: They come up by way of a ladder.

phrases.english: by way of the upper balcony to draw water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: בְּבָאִין בְּנֵי תַחְתּוֹנָה דֶּרֶךְ עֶלְיוֹנָה לְמַלּאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 1 by redefining the case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the lower balcony hoists water upward. In fact, both balconies draw by lowering from the upper level.

steps.title: The balconies are within ten טפחים, and the משנה uses a 'no need to say' style
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the balconies are within ten טפחים of each other. The משנה should be read as: obviously if only the lower one made a partition, both are forbidden, because being so close they forbid each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The case is where the balconies are within ten טפחים of each other, and the משנה is speaking in a 'no need to say' style. There is no need to say that if they made a partition for the lower one and not the upper one, they are forbidden. Since they are within ten טפחים of each other, they forbid each other.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second, different rejection of the proof. He says the balconies are very close, within ten טפחים, and he begins to explain how to read the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the balconies are this close, each side can easily use the other's space. So they forbid each other for that reason alone, whether they lower or hoist. The 'obvious' case is when only the lower one has a partition: then both draw by lowering through the same opening, so of course both are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no need to say: the obvious case, before the new point
They forbid it for one another

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think אביי is changing what the משנה says. He is only changing which case is the 'obvious' one. In his reading, the משנה's actual case (only the upper one has a partition) is the bigger חידוש, not the simple case.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
For example, where they stand within ten handbreadths of each other,
and the Mishnah is speaking in a 'no need to say' style:
There is no need to say that if they made a partition for the lower one
and did not make one for the upper one, they are forbidden,
because since they stand within ten handbreadths of each other,
they forbid it for one another,

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: כְּגוֹן דְּקַיָּימִין בְּתוֹךְ עֲשָׂרָה דַּהֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent rejection of the proof in step 1, instead of רב אדא בר אהבה's answer.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the reason for the prohibition was lowering versus hoisting. In fact, the reason is that the balconies are within ten טפחים of each other.

steps.title: The משנה's real point: even when only the upper one has a partition
steps.stepSummary: אביי finishes his reading. The משנה teaches that even when only the upper balcony has a partition, we do not give the space to the easy user, because balconies within ten טפחים forbid each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, even if they made a partition for the upper one and not for the lower one, you might have thought: since for this one it is easy and for that one it is hard, give it to the one whose use is easy. The משנה teaches us: since they are within ten טפחים, they forbid each other.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains the new point (חידוש) of the משנה in his reading. This finishes his rejection of the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might have applied שמואל's 'give it to the easy user' logic to the upper balcony. The משנה rules out that logic only when the balconies are within ten טפחים, because closeness alone makes them forbid each other. So when they are farther apart, שמואל's view could still stand, and the proof for רב falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought: introduces a rejected assumption
It teaches us: introduces the real point

steps.whatToRemember: There are two rejections of the proof for רב. According to רב אדא בר אהבה, both balconies draw by lowering. According to אביי, the balconies are within ten טפחים, so closeness makes them forbid each other. Either way, the משנה does not decide the lowering-versus-hoisting dispute.
steps.whyThisMatters: The case shows a basic method of the גמרא. A source can be pushed aside by finding a different reason for its ruling, so the ruling no longer depends on the disputed principle.

phrases.english: Rather, even if they made a partition for the upper one
and did not make one for the lower one,
it might have entered your mind to say:
since for this one its use is easy and for that one it is hard,
let it be given to the one whose use is easy,
so it teaches us:
since they stand within ten handbreadths,
they forbid it for one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ עָשׂוּ לָעֶלְיוֹנָה וְלֹא עָשׂוּ לַתַּחְתּוֹנָה, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes אביי's 'לא מיבעיא' reading begun in step 3 by stating the משנה's חידוש.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof for רב from the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's prohibition rests on closeness within ten טפחים, not on rejecting the 'easy user' principle in general.

steps.title: A roof near the public domain needs a fixed ladder
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up אביי's principle with שמואל's rule that a roof next to a רשות הרבים needs a fixed ladder. It explains that rule as working because the roof and the public domain are within ten טפחים of each other, so they forbid each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: a roof that is next to the public domain needs a fixed ladder to make it permitted. A fixed ladder works, but a temporary ladder does not. Why? Isn't it because the roof and the public domain are within ten טפחים of each other, so they forbid each other?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling of שמואל that seems to follow the same idea אביי just used. Two areas within ten טפחים of each other forbid each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The courtyard residents may use the roof only with a fixed ladder, which counts as a real doorway. A temporary ladder is not enough. The גמרא asks why a temporary ladder fails, and suggests this answer: the roof is within ten טפחים of the public domain, so both sides have easy access and block each other. Only a fixed ladder gives the courtyard a strong enough claim.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed, permanent ladder (treated like a real doorway)

steps.confusionAlert: The word לָאו here does not simply mean 'no.' It opens a leading question: 'Isn't it because...?' The גמרא is proposing a reason, not rejecting one.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Like that which Rav Naḥman said in the name of Shmuel:
phrases.notes: 'Like this' connects the coming ruling to אביי's principle.

phrases.english: A roof that is next to the public domain —
needs a fixed ladder to permit it.
phrases.notes: The courtyard residents may use the roof only with a permanent ladder.

phrases.aramaic: סוּלָּם קָבוּעַ אִין, סוּלָּם עֲרַאי לָא.
phrases.english: A fixed ladder, yes; a temporary ladder, no.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is reading this from the exact wording of the ruling.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Is it not because, since within ten [טפחים]
of each other they stand —
they forbid each other!

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's principle from Steps 3-4 with a parallel ruling of שמואל.
steps.raayaObject: The principle that spaces within ten טפחים of each other forbid each other, so the space is not given to the easy user
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב נחמן in the name of שמואל: a roof next to the public domain needs a fixed ladder

steps.title: Maybe the public puts hats and scarves on the roof
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rejects the proof. Maybe the fixed ladder is needed because the public actually uses the roof by resting their hats and scarves on it, not because of the ten-טפחים rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objected: But maybe this is a case where many people rest things on the roof, like their hats and scarves.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא knocks down the proof from Step 5. He offers a different reason why a fixed ladder is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the roof being within ten טפחים of the public domain. רב פפא says the roof may be higher than that. Even so, people walking by can still reach up and put light things on it, like hats and scarves. Because the public really uses it, the courtyard needs a fixed ladder. So שמואל's ruling does not prove אביי's ten-טפחים principle.

keyTerms.meaning: Rest or place things (as on a shoulder-height surface)

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the roof-and-ladder ruling fails. The fixed ladder may be needed only because the public actually uses the roof. So in the end, no clear proof was found for either רב or שמואל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the search for a proof. The disagreement stays open without any decisive source.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa objected to it:
But perhaps it is when the public rests things on it,
with a hat and a scarf.
phrases.notes: Light objects that are easy to place even on a higher roof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 5 by reinterpreting the case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from שמואל's ruling. It does not reject אביי's principle itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling can be explained by the public's actual use of the roof (placing hats and scarves), with no need for the ten-טפחים rule.

steps.title: A new statement of שמואל begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a new teaching that רב יהודה reports in the name of שמואל. The content comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל:
steps.whatsHappening: This line only sets up the next move. It introduces a new teaching whose words continue in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof discussion has ended, so the גמרא now moves to a fresh statement. Only the attribution appears here. The actual ruling will be explained on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא and student of שמואל, reporting his teacher's words
The early אמורא whose ruling is being reported
Formula for a teaching passed on from a teacher by his student

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
phrases.notes: What he actually said comes on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching after the proof discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ruling itself appears on the next amud.
